output.purpose: SWEny runs DAGs of coding-agent steps (Claude Code, Codex, pi, ACP agents) defined in YAML workflows, locally or in CI. It scopes each step's env and tools, validates output schemas, and records a receipt per run. For teams automating coding-agent work.
how_to_run: Use Node >=22, then run: npm install (installs all workspaces)
Run the CLI: node packages/core/dist/cli/main.js workflow run <file.yml> (the `sweny` bin)
In CI: use the GitHub Action swenyai/sweny@v5 (action.yml)
key_files: README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md: start here for the concepts and the contributor rules
packages/core/src/cli/: CLI entry point (main.js is built from here)
packages/core/src/schema.ts, types.ts, loader.ts: workflow definition and validation
packages/core/src/node-policy.ts, agent-env.ts, safe-outputs.ts, untrusted.ts: security scoping and output checks
packages/core/src/workflows/, .sweny/workflows/, examples/: built-in and sample workflows
action.yml and .github/workflows/ci.yml, release.yml: Action and CI/release
risks: Only Claude Code is fully supported. Codex, pi and ACP agents are experimental.
Every push to main triggers release.yml, which publishes to npm, so merges ship straight away. There are no changesets.
The build, test and run commands above come from a survey of the root scripts, not from running them. Check them against package.json.
The repo has many moving parts: 5 packages, 2 Astro sites, the plugin and the Action. Run builds from the repo root so workspaces resolve.
Security-sensitive code (env scoping, input fencing, output checks) needs careful review. Read SECURITY.md first.
